missing_requirements.title: Crash Recovery and Exam State Persistence
missing_requirements.description: The sandbox must persistently save exam state locally and safely handle unexpected OS crashes, forced reboots, or process termination without allowing bypass of the lockdown state upon restart.
missing_requirements.provenance: Exam integrity and fault tolerance domain standards
missing_requirements.justification: 1. If an OS crash occurs during an active exam session, the sandbox process terminates. 2. Without persistent local state and automatic lockdown re-initialization upon reboot, a student could exploit a deliberate crash to escape the sandbox environment. 3. Therefore, the system must enforce strict state persistence and re-apply display/clipboard restrictions immediately upon recovery to maintain security invariants.

missing_requirements.title: Anti-Tamper Process Watchdog and Debugger Detection
missing_requirements.description: The sandbox runtime must include a background watchdog mechanism to detect unauthorized debugging, memory injection, process termination attempts, or virtual machine instrumentation.
missing_requirements.justification: 1. A secure examination sandbox relies on continuous enforcement of clipboard and display restrictions. 2. Malicious users or advanced examinees may attempt to attach debuggers, terminate the sandbox watchdog process, or inject payloads to bypass hooks. 3. Therefore, anti-tamper safeguards and process monitoring are required to immediately terminate the exam session if tampering is detected.

missing_requirements.title: Hotkey and Global Shortcut Suppression
missing_requirements.description: The sandbox must intercept and suppress global OS shortcuts (e.g., Alt+Tab, Win+Shift+S, PrintScreen, Cmd+Tab, Cmd+Space) that permit window switching, screenshot capture, or Mission Control.
missing_requirements.provenance: Standard secure browser and examination lockdown specifications
missing_requirements.justification: 1. Restricting dual-monitors and clipboard paste alone is insufficient to prevent cheating if users can invoke native OS screenshot tools or switch to unauthorized windows. 2. Operating systems provide global keyboard shortcuts for task switching and screen capture by default. 3. Therefore, the sandbox must intercept and suppress these system-level hotkeys to ensure complete session containment.
